material.goal: Falsify the current RWO work-protocol boundary and return evidence-bounded requirements for a transport-neutral command/event adapter model that can map gRPC, sockets, Redis-backed queues, managed event buses, and memory without collapsing delivery behavior into lifecycle policy, journal truth, domain meaning, ARE reasoning, or effect authority.
material.context: This is one read-only review stage inside the parent-owned full Refine run. Inspect only the exact local sources named in each prompt. The parent has already frozen bounded official transport evidence in REFINE-SEED-PROPOSAL.md; agents must not browse. Returns are advisory attack receipts captured by the parent under the working folder. No product, ontology, runtime, definitions, telemetry, ledger, Git, external system, publication, promotion, deployment, authority, or production mutation is allowed. The review does not select an implementation; it tests abstractions, transport semantics, recovery identity, admission evidence, and owner boundaries before parent synthesis.

groups.anti_bias: methodology plus attack-vector: minimum protocol abstraction, heterogeneous transport failure semantics, and recovery-authority non-collapse

predicted_disagreements.statement: Agent 0 will prefer the smallest coherent port and profile structure, while agent 1 will reject any structure whose operations cannot truthfully represent incompatible acknowledgement, ordering, flow-control, reconnect, retry, and durability behavior across the five transport families; their disagreement tests abstraction economy versus semantic fidelity.

Agent 0 may place identity and admission fields in the shared adapter contract for coherence, while agent 2 will reject fields or operations that let an adapter substitute for journal acceptance, select a new Work Attempt, classify an unknown effect, inherit ARE evidence, or acquire authority; their disagreement tests interface completeness versus owner non-collapse.

Agent 1 may demand transport-specific observations and recovery hooks to preserve failure truth, while agent 2 will reject hooks that turn reconnect, redelivery, dead-letter, timeout, or duplicate signals into RWO recovery decisions or effect authorization; their disagreement tests operational observability versus decision authority.

agents.angle: adapter contract architect attacking over-generalization, lowest-common-denominator leakage, port coupling, envelope ambiguity, capability-profile incompleteness, and non-testable admission claims
